biological.citation: TAOK1 is associated with neurodevelopmental disorder and essential for neuronal maturation and cortical development (PMID: 33565190)
biological.summary: Altered TAOK1 expression levels in the embryonic mouse brain affect neural migration in vivo and neuronal maturation in vitro. A cohort of 23 individuals with mostly de novo TAOK1 variants showed a neurodevelopmental disorder comprising facial features, developmental delay/intellectual disability, muscular hypotonia, and feeding difficulties. Both truncating and missense variants were identified, with missense variants showing loss-of-function or dominant-negative effects.

biological.citation: Neurodevelopmental disorder-associated mutations in TAOK1 reveal its function as a plasma membrane remodeling kinase (PMID: 36595571)
biological.summary: TAOK1 is abundant in neurons in the mammalian brain and remodels the neuronal plasma membrane through direct association with phosphoinositides. Four NDD-associated TAOK1 mutations were catalytically inactive and aberrantly trapped in a membrane-bound state, inducing abnormal membrane protrusions and abnormal dendritic arbor growth in cultured mouse hippocampal neurons. Autophosphorylation of threonine-440 and threonine-443 in a triple-helical coiled-coil region blocks plasma membrane association of TAOK1.

biological.citation: Ste20-Like Kinase TAOK1 Positively Regulates Antiviral Responses by Controlling the TBK1-IRF3 Signaling Axis (PMID: 36649698)
biological.summary: TAOK1 positively regulates virus-induced type I interferon production by promoting TBK1-IRF3 complex formation in a kinase activity-dependent manner. TAOK1 is constitutively associated with TBK1 independently of MAVS, and viral infection induces TAOK1 to bind dynein instead of MAP4, trafficking TBK1 along microtubules to the perinuclear region to bind IRF3. TAOK1 deficiency decreased nucleic acid-mediated type I IFN production and increased susceptibility to virus infection.

biological.citation: TAOK1 negatively regulates IL-17-mediated signaling and inflammation (PMID: 29400705)
biological.summary: TAOK1 functions as a negative regulator of IL-17-mediated signal transduction by interacting with IL-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) independent of its kinase activity, dose-dependently preventing formation of the IL-17R-Act1 complex. TAOK1 knockdown promoted IL-17-induced cytokine/chemokine expression and activation of MAPK and NF-κB. TAOK1 deficiency exacerbated colitis in a TNBS-induced inflammatory bowel disease model, and TAOK1 expression was decreased in colons of ulcerative colitis patients.

biological.citation: TAOK1 promotes filament formation in HR repair through phosphorylating USP7 (PMID: 40106350)
biological.summary: TAOK1 plays a pivotal role in the DNA damage response by phosphorylating USP7, thereby promoting its enzymatic activity and preventing ubiquitylation and degradation of RAD51, a crucial protein in homologous recombination (HR) repair filament formation. Genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition of TAOK1 impaired USP7 function, leading to RAD51 degradation, disruption of HR repair, and increased tumor cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition. This identifies TAOK1 as a critical regulator of the HR repair pathway and a potential target to overcome PARP inhibitor resistance.

biological.citation: Thousand and one amino acid protein kinase 1 suppression improves doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by preventing cardiomyocyte death and dysfunction (PMID: 39964965)
biological.summary: A kinome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) identified TAOK1 as a regulator of doxorubicin-induced cardiomyocyte death. TAOK1 suppression improved DOX-induced cardiomyocyte death, sarcomere disarray, contractile dysfunction, DNA damage, and mitochondrial dysfunction via attenuation of p38 MAPK activation. AAV-mediated TAOK1 silencing in mice attenuated DOX-induced myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis, and cardiomyocyte atrophy, improving cardiac function.

biological.citation: Silencing of STE20-type kinase TAOK1 confers protection against hepatocellular lipotoxicity through metabolic rewiring (PMID: 36930872)
biological.summary: TAOK1 mRNA expression in human liver biopsies positively correlated with key hallmarks of NAFLD including hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and ballooning in a cohort of 62 participants. TAOK1 protein fully colocalized with intracellular lipid droplets in human and mouse hepatocytes. TAOK1 silencing alleviated lipotoxicity by accelerating lipid catabolism, suppressing lipid anabolism, and mitigating oxidative/ER stress, while TAOK1 knockdown inhibited ERK and JNK activation and repressed acetyl-CoA carboxylase abundance.

biological.citation: A global phosphosite-correlated network map of Thousand And One Kinase 1 (TAOK1) (PMID: 38479581)
biological.summary: Analysis of 709 qualitative and 210 quantitative differential cellular phosphoproteome datasets identified Ser421, Ser9, Ser965, and Ser445 as the predominant TAOK1 phosphosites, representing TAOK1 in ~75% of datasets. TAOK1 is described as a core member of the Hippo signaling pathway and is linked to microtubule dynamics, checkpoint signaling, and DNA damage response. pSer9 is proposed as an autophosphorylation and kinase activity-associated site, while pSer421 is proposed as a regulatory phosphosite involved in genome integrity maintenance.

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - Novel de novo TAOK1 variants associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype, macrocephaly, and joint hypermobility (H.M. McLaughlin et al.)
biological.summary: Six individuals with novel de novo heterozygous TAOK1 variants were identified from 9,302 exome cases with neurodevelopmental phenotypes, with a seventh identified through GeneMatcher. Variant types included missense, nonsense, frameshift, and splice site variants, suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance. Clinical features included intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, language and motor delays, hypotonia, macrocephaly, and joint hypermobility, representing the first report of de novo TAOK1 variants causing human disease.

biological.citation: A Genome- and Phenome-Wide Association Study to Identify Genetic Variants Influencing Platelet Count and Volume and their Pleiotropic Effects - ASHG 2012 (K. Shameer et al.)
biological.summary: A GWAS in 13,582 participants of European ancestry identified TAOK1 among genes in chromosomal regions associated with platelet count (PLT) and mean platelet volume (MPV). TAOK1 was listed among kinase-encoding genes in these regions, implicating it in thrombopoiesis. PheWAS analysis revealed pleiotropic effects of variants in these regions associated with autoimmune diseases, hematologic disorders, hypothyroidism, and myocardial infarction.
